**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred level) — no redline proposed.**

The only exclusivity mechanic in the Agreement, Section 5.8 (p0368–p0369), binds Harpoon (counterparty), not us: Harpoon and its Affiliates may not develop, commercialize or enable any Third Party to exploit a Competing Product in the Territory. The Acquisition / Change-in-Control carve-out at 5.8.2 is conditioned on the acquirer Segregating the Competing Product and preserves AbbVie's unilateral right to shut off delivery of its Confidential Information and disband the JGC — so our position is protected.

I checked for any reciprocal duty on AbbVie (sole-supplier, requirements purchasing, "AbbVie shall not", non-compete, supply obligations) and found none. AbbVie instead holds the sole right to Manufacture/have Manufactured and supply (4.5.1), free appointment of distributors (5.4) and co-promotion partners (5.5), and multi-tier sublicensing (5.3). Exclusivity running in Customer's favour is expressly acceptable under this rule, so the preferred element — no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer — is already met.
